messages:
omar: Quick thread 20m sync: customer asked for guaranteed outbound IP stability for private endpoints even during control-plane failovers. They9re on our private endpoint model. Thoughts?
rachel: If endpoint lives in our VPC we NAT -> they see our egress IP. Guaranteeing the same IP across failovers implies reserving stable egress addresses per-tenant or using a relay inside customer VPC.
kevin: We discussed options before: 1) per-tenant static pool 2) per-tenant NAT instances/ENIs 3) eBPF-based hairpin preserving internal source (requires placement in customer network) 4) documented IP rotation with short TTL.
sue: ENI per tenant is simplest from correctness POV but $$$ and provisioning overhead. Static pool as an add-on seems reasonable: small set of public IPs assigned to tenant and rotated rarely.
ethan: Implementation nuance: for graceful failover we need session handoff of NAT mappings or keepalive proxy. Otherwise TCP sessions break and golang clients will reconnect from new TCP 5-tuple -> backend rejects.
omar: Is there a cheap way to do lease-based stable IPs without full ENI?
kevin: We could allocate a tiny managed NAT pool per tenant and implement sticky allocation in the dataplane. Leases map internal flows to egress IP:port. On failover we stream compact diffs to target relay. Needs reliable handoff channel and small window for races.
rachel: Streaming diffs + sequence numbers seems doable. But how to handle long-lived flows (>lease TTL)? We either extend leases or route those flows to original node (hard).
sue: Question: do we need zero-downtime for all customers? Maybe offer two SKUs: "Best-effort" (no guarantees) and "IP-stable" (paid, with the managed pool + SLAs). That reduces scope.
ethan: Rollout: phase 1 design RFC for dataplane lease format + handoff API. Phase 2 smoke tests in staging: simulate relay failover and verify egress IP stability for 95% flows. Phase 3 pilot with a willing customer.
omar: Security: make sure handoff bundles are signed and authenticated. Don9t want leaked lease data to reassign IPs.
kevin: Also need observability: per-tenant egress metrics, current lease counts, conflicts. Add to Console as a toggle for Private endpoints.
rachel: Cost model: small pool (2-4 addresses) per tenant priced monthly. Compute cost estimate: NAT bandwidth + IP cost + extra routing complexity. Sue, Ethan could you do pricing spreadsheet?
sue: On it. Will include ENI vs managed pool vs relay-in-customer-vpc.
ethan: infra-bot: started e2e simulation job: nat-lease-handoff-sim -> staging (ETA 18m) :rocket:
omar: Decision for now: offer IP-stable as an opt-in add-on for Private endpoints. Nora/Kevin to produce short RFC outlining lease format, handoff API (/v1/relays/handoff), auth model, and rollback semantics. Sue/Ethan to run cost sheet and pilot checklist.
sue: ack
kevin: I'll take the RFC draft. Will include example protobuf for lease bundle and a small state machine for handoff.
omar: Thanks all. If no objections within 24h we'll ship the RFC and start the staging tests.
